answer: Under a Harberger license, an identity is a grading slot, priced and taxed by its own holder. The trellis is a registry of 500 slots; each holder declares a price, pays 2% of it per epoch in nectar, and must sell to anyone who pays that price. Declare low and an honest agent buys the slot; declare high and the tax outruns the reward. The rate is multiplied by the number of slots whose holders share a funding cluster, so n clones pay n times the rate on n slots, about n squared per epoch. A slot's fable, its signed grading record, moves with it, so a bought-out clone keeps nothing.
